discussion_comments.comment_body: Leaving this out on purpose. Counting spawns in a unit test would mean mocking `node:child_process`, which breaks the promisified `execFile` (`.child` / `{ stdout }`), or putting a shell-script `git` wrapper on PATH, which won't work on Windows. We try not to add test-only plumbing like that. The process counts were checked against real checkpoints instead: CLI and VS Code sessions on a repo with 3,000 untracked files. main peaked at 3,051 concurrent git processes and 3,046 zombies for one comparison; this branch uses 6 git processes in total per comparison. The existing tests still cover correctness for both the tracked and the third-parent lookups.

**[P2] Apply provisioning suppression to the combined loader condition.** On a new cloud send, `beginPendingResponse` sets the optimistic marker. The coordinator emits `cloud_provisioning` through the partial-message stream before the full-state acknowledgement arrives; partial messages leave `turnState` unchanged, and that acknowledgement goes through the 50 ms state-post debounce. During this handoff, `forceShow` is still true and the provisioning message has `partial: false`, so `optimisticShow` below overrides this `false` and renders “Thinking…” alongside the progress card. This contradicts the intended suppression and adds an avoidable loader insertion/removal at startup.

Gate the combined condition passed to `useDebouncedLoaderVisibility` on the provisioning tail, keeping the hook call unconditional. The added helper-only test misses this: rendering the full hook with a provisioning tail, stale idle `turnState`, and `forceShow: true` currently returns visible. Cover that combination, then verify an `api_req_started` successor can show the loader again.

Good catch, thanks. Fixed in f8d9ca206: the provisioning check now gates the combined condition passed to `useDebouncedLoaderVisibility` (`!cloudProvisioning && (optimisticShow || isWaitingForResponse || handoffToReasoningPending)`), and the hook call stays unconditional. I moved the check out of `computeIsWaitingForResponse` instead of duplicating it, so that helper matches main again.

I replaced the helper-only test with a full-hook test: a provisioning tail, a stale idle `turnState`, and `forceShow: true` keep the loader hidden, then an `api_req_started` successor shows it again. The test fails on the previous code (`expected true to be false`) and passes with the fix.

Valid, added. `skills-cli.test.ts` checks the exported value against core's `package.json`: the devDependency must be an exact `x.y.z` (no tag or range) and `SKILLS_CLI_VERSION` / `SKILLS_CLI_PACKAGE` must equal it. I checked that hardcoding `"skills@latest"` back into the constant makes it fail. The call-site tests keep using the constant, as you suggested.

Not adding tests here. This PR is one log call on the existing socket close path (the connection.closed line you mention was in an earlier revision and is gone). Asserting on the shape of an info log line would mean enabling hub logging in vitest and spying on console output to lock down field names, which is more harness than the change is worth and would make future edits to the log payload churn tests for no behavioral gain. The close path itself is already exercised by the existing server tests, which is what would catch a real regression.
